name: Hardcore Feijoada

ingredients.name: green bell pepper, core and seeds discarded, diced fine

instructions.primary_message: Dissolve 1/4 cup kosher salt in a gallon of cold water. Add the beans and allow to soak overnight (at least 8 hours). Drain and rinse.

Combine soaked beans, pork parts, sausage, beef, onion, pepper, scallion, cilantro, tomato, and bay leaves in a large saucepot. Cover with water by 5 cm. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a simmer and cook, topping up with water as necessary to keep beans completely submerged until beans are completely tender and liquid is a deep black, about 6 to 8 hours. Season to taste with salt (you probably won't need any more, depending on how salty your pig parts were). Serve with rice, orange wedges, greens, hot sauce, and farofa. Feijoada is excellent reheated.

schema_metadata.keywords: beans, Brazil, Brazilian, feijoada, pork, South America

description: Our recipe for the national dish of Brazil features slow-cooked black beans and a panoply of fresh and salted meats.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 14 hr 20 min.

Optional or for serving: 0.23 kg carne do sol or corned beef, cut into 1.5 to 2.5-cm chunks (optional)

Optional substitutions: Sautéed kale → shredded cabbage

Notes: For best results, use as many different salted pork parts as available, though you can always make it with just a few. Straight up salt pork and slab bacon with some good sausage will be quite delicious.
Farofa is fried manioc (yucca) flour. It can be found in Brazilian markets ready-to-eat, or make it yourself by toasted rough-ground yucca flour in a bit of oil in a skillet over medium heat until golden brown.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
